recipes.name: My Special Shrimp Scampi Florentine
ingredients_raw: 2 large plum tomatoes, seeded and diced
2 tablespoons prepared basil pesto (such as Classico ™)
0.25 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste
1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 cups fresh spinach, rinsed and stemmed

steps.text: Combine butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in tomatoes, pesto, and garlic; simmer until tomatoes start to soften, about 2 minutes. Season with pepper flakes and black pepper.
Stir shrimp into sauce; cook just until they turn pink, 3 to 5 minutes. Add spinach; stir until wilted, about 1 minute.

raw_recipe.headline: My Special Shrimp Scampi Florentine
raw_recipe.description: My special shrimp scampi Florentine recipe has the fresh flavors of tomatoes, fresh spinach, and pesto. Serve it over rice with hot Italian bread.

review.reviewBody: What an oily, buttery, fattening MESS! This was good, but good grief! The main sauce ingredients were oil, butter and more oil! I halved those ingredients and added some Chardonnay with a bit of corn starch to thicken it up a bit. I also added the juice of 1/2 a lemon. I am soooo glad I did! I can't imagine this otherwise! Don't get me wrong, this was very good, but with a few alterations.

I made this with a few changes which take a little extra time but so worth it! If using shell on shrimp, simmer the shrimp shells in white wine for about 10 minutes. Remove shrimp shells and use the wine reduction for part of the liquids, reducing the butter and oil. I didn't have pesto on hand so just used basil. I used mini penne and added to pan with most of a bag of spinach. Perfect with a sprinkling of parmesan on top of each serving!

I consider myself to be a scampi snob & I loved this. I had to make some modifications based on what I had on hand. I cut the butter to 1/4 c, added 1T lemon juice & 1/4 c of pinot Grigio. I used frozen cooked shrimp which I thawed ahead of time & cherry tomatoes that I cut in half. After sauteeing the garlic & spices, I added the shrimp, tomatoes & spinach all at once & cooked til heated through. Served over linguini & it was truly scrumptious. Update: I have to laugh as this was in my "favorites" & I didn't remember I had already made it. This time, I followed the recipe (no added wine or lemon juice) but I added 1/4 c. Chopped red onion & 4 oz sliced mushrooms at the beginning. It was truly delicious made this way! 5 stars again!

Making this for the second time and I must say it is by far the best tasting shrimp dish I've ever made!!!!
Simple, quick, and absolutely delicious!!
I did however forego the "prepared basil pesto" and used fresh, chopped, dried basil from my garden, about 3 tablespoons, and added a little (1/4 cup) cooking wine, and a squish (1/3 of a lg lemon) of fresh lemon juice. - KO'

I took the advice from a rating that it was too oily and cut back the butter and oil and added some white wine. It still was very oily so my recommendation would be to serve it with a plain rice (I served risotto) or pasta to spread out some of that oil. I added lots of garlic and some jalapeño peppers and sweet peppers and onion. It was very good, enjoyed by everyone.

Great flavor. I used shallots and portabellos I had on hand. Big switch really paid off: I used Sun Dried Tomato pesto instead of the usual basil-based. Too much better.
I also added oven crisped prosciutto crumbles. Be careful with the crush red pepper flakes though.... Thanks for sharing this recipe.

I made the recipe exactly as written. Pretty to look at; bland in taste. I would make this again with my own adjustments, such as, bumping up the chili flakes to 1/2 teaspoon and the fresh spinach to 3 cups, adding salt to taste, and using oil-packed julienned tomatoes. The fresh plum tomatoes tasted too anemic for such an elegant dish.

Minimal effort for fine Italian restaurant quality. I scaled this down to two servings (just for myself). This comes together VERY quickly. After reading reviews, I further cut back by half on the oil and butter (~1 tblsp each). My small shrimp were frozen-cooked, so I thawed and cooked just until heated. I didn't want to open a jar of pesto sauce, so I just used dried basil. Nice bite from the red pepper flakes; used regular tomatoes. I also added a splash of white wine, and I found that it does need salt. I had as-is (no pasta), so that was a nice, low-carb treat! Definite keeper recipe!

I took the advice of other reviewers and only used 2 tbs. each of butter and olive oil. I did add more pesto (approx. 4 tbs.) and didn't add any additional garlic. With the pesto, there was plenty of garlic. I used a whole bag of baby spinach, an additional tomato, and 2 lbs. of shrimp and there was plenty of sauce. Served over brown rice it was delicious! I think the suggestion of thickening the sauce with a bit of cornstarch and water would make it even more amazing. I will definitely make this again!

Very Good! I Was looking to use up some shrimp & fresh spinach I had on hand so this worked perfectly. I did cut the butter & oil in half. And I added a little salt & pepper. I didn't use any red pepper.

One of the best recipes I’ve tried in a long time. Following others suggestions, I reduced the oil to 1T, increased pesto to 3T and added 1/2c vermouth that I had first simmered with shrimp shells. I also added 5oz of fresh spinach that I roughly chopped. Served over rice. So good the two of us ate it all.
Excellent! Easy, quick, tasty and it was complete with veggies. I used mixed greens and we had it over rice. I'll keep this one.
This recipe was really easy to make and very tasty. I added the juice of one lemon and a cup of white wine and garnished with grated cheese and parsley; very yummy.
I added sliced onions instead of tomatoes which 2 of my family dislikes. It was easy to make. Will make it again.
Followed the recipe, without measuring. I did add lemon juice. Overall very good.
This was so good I didn't want to stop eating it! Normally I make changes to recipes, but I didn't do that with this one. I did serve it over pasta though. Definitely will keep it in my rotation!
DIsappointed overall. Followed some of the suggestion-extra spinach. Soaked shrimp shells in white wine and added. Cut back on butter and oil.. Just thought it was bland. Served over rice.
I doubled this and served it at a dinner party and it was a big hit! Colorful, easy and not so much time in the kitchen. Didn't have prepared pesto, but I did have fresh basil so I used that instead.
Made it several times exactly according to the recipe. It is delish!

This was the bomb! My husband raved about how delicious it was! The only modifications I mad was to add about a 1/2 cup of savignoin white wine and I added the red pepper flakes to each finished dis as not everyone in the house can handle that heat. I will be making this again, and again! Thank you’
